_meta.description: Document-rules config for lease_deed — LONG-TERM lease (> 11 months OR with renewal extending beyond 11 months) under Transfer of Property Act 1882 S.105-117. Distinct from rent_agreement.json (which targets <= 11 months unregistered short-term). Mandatory registration per Registration Act S.17(d). Cites Anthony v. K.C. Ittoop & Sons (2000) 6 SCC 394.
_meta.change_protocol: All edits require CLO sign-off. If user data shows tenure <= 11 months without renewal — auto-route to rent_agreement template.

promptInstructions: Draft a LEASE DEED for LONG-TERM lease (term > 11 months) under Transfer of Property Act, 1882, Sections 105 to 117.

S.105 TPA — Definition: A lease of immovable property is a transfer of a right to enjoy such property, made for a certain time, express or implied, or in perpetuity, in consideration of a price paid or promised, or of money, a share of crops, service or any other thing of value, to be rendered periodically or on specified occasions to the transferor by the transferee, who accepts the transfer on such terms.

S.107 TPA — Mode: A lease of immovable property from year to year, or for any term exceeding ONE YEAR, or reserving a yearly rent, can be made ONLY by a REGISTERED INSTRUMENT. All other leases may be made either by a registered instrument or by oral agreement accompanied by delivery of possession.
S.17(1)(d) REGISTRATION ACT — Leases of immovable property from year to year, or for any term exceeding ONE YEAR, or reserving a yearly rent, MUST be registered.

STAMP DUTY: state-specific schedules — depends on annual rent + security deposit + lease tenure. Rough indicators (verify current rates):
   - Bihar: 1% of average annual rent + premium for terms up to 10 years; higher for longer; + 2% registration.
   - Jharkhand: similar — % of total rent payable over term.
   - UP: 4% of average annual rent for term up to 10 years; sliding scale for longer; + 1% registration.
   - Delhi: 2% of average annual rent + advance + premium for terms up to 5 years; 3% for 5-10 years; 5% for > 10 years.
   DO NOT hardcode — flag advocate to verify.

Cite Anthony v. K.C. Ittoop & Sons (2000) 6 SCC 394 — even where a deed of lease for a term exceeding one year is unregistered, possession and rent receipts may create a year-to-year tenancy under S.107 second paragraph; however, the registered deed's specific terms (renewal, options) cannot be enforced from an unregistered deed.
Cite Anthony Lawrence v. Pridhi (1985) 1 SCC 469 (where applicable) — for principles of forfeiture and re-entry.
STRUCTURE OF DEED:
Para 1: Parties — full identification including PAN, Aadhaar (last 4), business identity for entities (CIN for company, GSTIN, registered office).
Para 2: Recital — Lessor is absolute owner of demise; chain of title.

Para 3: Demise / Habendum — 'Lessor doth hereby demise and lease unto Lessee ALL THAT property more fully described in Schedule A...TO HOLD the same unto the Lessee for the term of {X} years commencing from {start_date} and ending on {end_date}'.
Para 4: Reddendum — 'YIELDING AND PAYING therefor monthly rent of Rs. {monthly_rent} payable in advance on or before the {N}th day of each English calendar month...'.
Para 5: Rent escalation — 'The said monthly rent shall be enhanced by {X}% on each anniversary of the commencement date, the enhanced rent being calculated on the immediately preceding rent.'
Para 6: Security deposit — interest-free / interest-bearing, refundable on vacation subject to deductions for arrears, damages, dues.
Para 7: Lock-in period — if applicable, lessee cannot terminate before lock-in; lessor's right to forfeit deposit / claim balance lock-in rent specified.
Para 8: Permitted use — narrow definition; no other use without consent.
Para 11: Maintenance allocation — major/structural to lessor, day-to-day to lessee unless varied.
Para 12: Subletting / Assignment — usually barred / conditional. Where commercial — permitted to affiliates only.
Para 13: Alterations / Fit-out — with prior written consent; lessee to restore on exit (cost from deposit) unless waived.
Para 14: Termination — (a) Notice — typically 3-6 months for commercial; (b) Default — non-payment cure period; (c) Forfeiture per S.111 TPA grounds; (d) Force majeure clause.

Para 15: S.111 TPA — Determination of lease: by efflux of time, by happening of specified event, on termination of lessor's interest, merger, express surrender, implied surrender, forfeiture, notice to quit.
Para 16: Holdover — if lessee continues after term expiry, holdover rent (typically 1.5x or 2x) applies; tenancy at sufferance.
Para 17: Dispute resolution — arbitration clause (institutional or ad-hoc) under Arbitration & Conciliation Act 1996; seat / venue specified.
Para 18: Governing law and jurisdiction.
Para 19: TDS clause — Lessee shall deduct TDS u/s 194-I (corporate lessee, rent > Rs.2.4L/year) or 194-IB (individual lessee, rent > Rs.50K/month) and remit; issue Form 16A.
Para 20: GST clause — if commercial lease and lessor's turnover > GST threshold OR reverse charge applies; lessee to pay GST in addition to rent.
Para 21: Registration — parties acknowledge mandatory registration; stamp duty + registration fee borne by [specified party].
Schedule A — property description.
Two witnesses' attestation.
Append Lawie disclaimer.

Where commercial lease — additional clauses for fit-out period (rent-free period during fit-out), rent commencement date distinct from possession date, hand-over conditions, anti-corruption / anti-bribery, confidentiality, indemnity caps.
Where lessor is HUF — Karta executes with consent of adult coparceners.
Where lessor is a company — board resolution required and annexed.

filing_checklist: Stamp paper of correct denomination (state schedule based on average annual rent + advance + tenure)
Lessor's title documents for SR inspection
Encumbrance Certificate (EC) — past 13 years
Approved plan / Occupancy Certificate (for built-up structures)
Property tax receipts up to date
Society / RWA NOC if applicable
Where Lessor is HUF — Karta + adult coparceners' consent
Where Lessor is company — Board Resolution + MOA + Authorised Signatory PoA
Where Lessee is company — Board Resolution + Authorised Signatory PoA
PAN of both parties
Aadhaar of both parties (individuals)
GST registration certificate (where commercial lease)
Two adult witnesses with own ID proofs
Both parties physically present at Sub-Registrar for registration
2 passport-size photographs each
Registration within 4 months of execution (S.23 Registration Act)
Post-registration: TDS compliance by Lessee (Form 26QC for 194-IB / Form 26Q for 194-I)
Where rent control state — verify whether premises within Rent Control Act ambit; if yes, special procedure
Where commercial lease > Rs.18,000/month — GST registration of Lessor (if applicable) and proper invoicing
Lawie disclaimer included
validation_rules: lease_term_years + lease_term_months/12 must be > 11 months — otherwise route to rent_agreement template
if lease_term_years > 1 OR rent is yearly — registration mandatory under S.17(1)(d) Registration Act; flag
security_deposit > 0 and typically <= 6 months' rent (Model Tenancy Act benchmark)
if monthly_rent_initial > 50000 and lessee_is_entity == 'individual' — flag TDS u/s 194-IB
if lessee_is_entity in ['company_pvt_ltd_or_ltd', 'partnership', 'llp'] and (monthly_rent_initial * 12) > 240000 — flag TDS u/s 194-I
